approved: Recycling and Waste Reduction Charges (General) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package of three bills that would allow the Commonwealth to recover the costs of regulating waste exports.
The bills would create a framework for imposing charges, but the amounts and who pays them would be set later in regulations made by the Governor-General.
Three separate bills are needed because the Constitution requires excise, customs and other taxation to be in separate Acts.
Enable the Commonwealth to recover costs of regulating certain waste material exports.
Provide a framework for imposing charges, with amounts set by future regulations.
Ensure appropriate cost recovery mechanisms for Commonwealth services related to regulated waste material.
Exporters of regulated waste materials and the Commonwealth Government.

The Recycling and Waste Reduction Charges (General) Bill 2020 enables cost recovery for administering the waste export ban, which phases out exports of waste glass from 1 January 2021, mixed plastics from 1 July 2021, whole used tyres from 1 December 2021, single polymer plastics from 1 July 2022, and mixed paper and cardboard from 1 July 2024.
The Recycling and Waste Reduction Charges (Customs) Bill 2020 imposes customs duties as part of the waste export ban charging package, with charge amounts and liable parties to be set by regulation.

The Recycling and Waste Reduction Charges (Excise) Bill 2020 was moved for a second reading, forming part of the waste export ban charging legislative package. It imposes charges only when considered a duty of excise, with amounts and exemptions to be set in regulations, and does not itself set charge amounts or impose financial impacts.

The speaker moved to rescind the third readings of five recycling and waste reduction bills and to immediately call them on again, with a Minister moving each third reading and the question put without debate.
